Home.heroTitle: Check an address before you send
Home.heroSub: Paste an address — we'll show the risk and why.
Home.requestsKinds: Address checks, token analyses, whale and sanctions searches
Home.requestsChartAria: Requests per day over the last 14 days
Home.howStep1Text: A wallet address, a token contract or a .eth name, and pick the network: Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Tron, Bitcoin and more. No sign-up, no wallet connection.
Home.howStep2Text: A few seconds later: a number from 0 to 100 and a risk level. We look at sanctions lists, Tether and Circle freezes, hack and phishing labels and links to flagged addresses.
Home.howStep3Text: Under the score you see what it is made of, and every label comes with its source and a link. The decision stays with you.
Home.howTip: Before a large transfer compare the address character by character and send a small test amount first. 'Low risk' means no known signals, not that the address is safe.
Home.frozenText: Addresses the issuers blocked recently. USDT and USDC sent to such an address may become unreachable.
Home.faq1a: Yes. No sign-up, no subscription and no wallet connection.
Home.faq2q: If the score is low, is it safe to send?
Home.faq2a: A low score means there are no known signals. It is not a guarantee of safety: new schemes and new addresses may not be known yet. Compare the address character by character and send a small test amount first.
Home.faq3q: Where does the data come from?
Home.faq3a: From open sources: the US (OFAC), UK and EU sanctions lists, Tether and Circle blocking events read from the blockchains themselves, labels of hacks, phishing and scams from open datasets, plus our own database and a check at the moment of the request. Every label on a check page shows its source with a link.
Home.faq4a: Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Polygon, Optimism, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Tron and Bitcoin. Tron and Bitcoin are checked in a reduced scope: lists, open databases and the latest transfers, without deep tracing.
Home.faq5q: What if I already sent money to a risky address?
Home.faq5a: Save the transaction hash, contact the support of the exchange or wallet, the police and the platform where you were deceived. Do not pay "recovery services": they are a common second scam. Only the issuer can release frozen USDT or USDC.
Home.faq6q: Do you store the addresses I check?
Home.faq6a: Yes: we store the address, the network and the result to see what is searched most. Crypto addresses are public, the record is not tied to your identity, and we do not store IP addresses. If you type anything other than an address, it is not stored.
Home.faq7a: No. It is an automatic risk signal based on open data. An address may be listed by mistake; if you see an error, every check has a link "Wrong score? Tell us" at the bottom.
Home.levelsNote: Scores are automatic. Not an accusation.

faq.a: Usually one address or a transaction hash and a short description of the situation are enough. We clarify the rest in the correspondence.

faq.q: Will you get my money back?
faq.a: No. We do not recover funds and we do not take a prepayment for a "recovery". We show where the money went and prepare material for a request to an exchange, a platform or a court. Beware of people who write to a victim first and promise to get the money back for a fee: that is a scam of its own.

faq.q: Can the report be attached to a complaint or a claim?
faq.a: The report is written so that a lawyer can use it easily: every conclusion has a source. It is an informational document, and whether it is admissible as evidence is up to a lawyer and the court.
We name the price before the work starts, after a short discussion of the task. A dossier on an address and the tracing of a small amount cost less than a project investigation.
We do not publish the details of your task. If needed, we will sign a non-disclosure agreement.

faq.q: Do you reveal who owns an address?
faq.a: No. We work with open and official data and do not promise to establish an identity. If there is public information about an address (an ENS name, mentions, labels), we give it with sources and neutral wording.

Terms.title: Terms of use
Terms.metaDescription: SpiderAML terms of use: a free information service; the risk score is automatic, based on public data, and is not legal advice.
Terms.privacy: How we handle data — see the privacy policy →
sections: What SpiderAML is

SpiderAML is a free information service. It collects what official sanctions lists and public databases say about crypto addresses and presents it in plain language. By using the site you agree to these terms.
Not a verdict and not an accusation

The risk score is produced automatically. It is not legal, tax or financial advice and not a statement that the owner of an address did anything unlawful. Addresses end up in databases by mistake, and new schemes may not be in any database yet. Low risk does not guarantee safety.
Data “as is”

We show third-party data as it was published and name the source next to every signal. We are not responsible for its completeness, accuracy or freshness, or for decisions made on the basis of the score. The sources and their terms are listed below.
Sanctions
A “sanctions list” mark only means the address appears in a list published by a regulator. Whether sanctions apply to you and how to comply is your responsibility; ask a lawyer if in doubt.
If an address is flagged by mistake

Tell us through the Report form (“This is a mistake”) or by email. We will review it and remove SpiderAML's own label if it is wrong. We cannot change official sanctions lists or other parties' databases, but we will tell you whom to contact.
Safe send
The Safe send section runs on the Arbitrum Sepolia testnet; the money there is not real. The SpiderSend contract never holds funds; your wallet makes the transfers and you confirm them yourself.
What is not allowed
Do not scrape the site automatically, work around rate limits, disrupt the service, or present a SpiderAML score as an official decision of a regulator.
Changes
We may update the service and these terms; the date of the last change is shown at the top.

Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.metaDescription: What data SpiderAML collects and why: checked addresses, anonymous visit statistics and your analytics choice.
sections: In short

There is no sign-up. We do not ask for your name, email or phone, do not store IP addresses and use no advertising cookies. We turn on Google Analytics only if you agree in the banner; until then nothing from Google is loaded.
Telegram bot

If you use our Telegram bot, we store your numeric Telegram ID (not your name or username), the interface language and, for each check, the address, the network and the result, to count usage and to protect the paid lookups from abuse. This is a link between an ID and an address, kept for a limited time. Write to us to have it deleted.
Visit statistics

To see what is used, we record: which page was opened and what was clicked; the site you came from (domain only) or a link tag such as ?src=telegram; the device type (phone or computer); the country, as reported by Cloudflare. A visitor is identified for one day by a hash of a random “salt”, the IP address and the browser; the salt is deleted the next day, so visits on different days cannot be linked and the record cannot identify a person. Records older than 13 months are deleted automatically.
Google Analytics (only with your consent)

If you click “Accept”, Google Analytics 4 is switched on. It sets cookies, infers an approximate location and device type, and sends Google which pages were opened and when. The page address is sent without its parameters, so the addresses you check never reach Google. Advertising features and personalisation are off. You can withdraw consent at any time with the “Cookie settings” button at the bottom of the page: Google then stops receiving data and its cookies are deleted.
Checked addresses

When you check an address or a token we store the address, the network and the result, to see what people look for most. Crypto addresses are public; the record is not tied to your identity. To run the check our server sends the address (not your data) to external services: GoPlus, Zerion, CoinGecko, Etherscan, a blockchain node provider and, for Bitcoin addresses, mempool.space and Blockstream. If you type something other than an address (an e-mail or a name, say), it is not stored: only a marker and the length of the text are recorded.
Address reports

The Report form stores the address, network, category, your description and the link. We do not ask for contact details — please do not put personal data in the description. Only the SpiderAML team sees the report; its status opens through a secret link that only you receive.
Cookies and browser storage

The site remembers your chosen language in one cookie (NEXT_LOCALE) for a year, and your answer about analytics in the browser's local storage. If you allowed Google Analytics, Google sets its own cookies (_ga…); if you decline we delete them. In Safe send your browser remembers that a wallet was connected; this stays on your device. We never receive your wallet, keys or signatures.
Who else handles traffic

The site runs behind Cloudflare (protection and delivery) on a Hetzner server in the European Union. Cloudflare sees technical request data under its own privacy policy. If you agreed to analytics, Google also receives data about your visit.
Your rights
You can ask us to delete a report you sent or ask about your data — write to us. Since we do not know who you are, include the report's status link.

Consent.title: Cookies and analytics
Consent.text: We would like to count visits with Google Analytics: it sets cookies and sends data to Google. Nothing from Google is loaded until you agree. Only the pages you open are sent, never the addresses you check.

Frozen.title: Frozen USDT and USDC addresses
Frozen.sub: Check whether a wallet is frozen: addresses that Tether and Circle have blocked in their contracts.
Frozen.metaDescription: Frozen USDT and USDC addresses: check if a wallet is blocked by Tether or Circle. Network, freeze date and transaction link. Search by address.
Frozen.note: A freeze is the issuer's decision (Tether or Circle) to block the tokens on an address. It is not proof of a crime: the issuer does not give a reason, and an address can be released. The list is built from the events of the USDT and USDC contracts.
Frozen.verdictFrozen: This address is on an issuer blacklist
Frozen.verdictClear: Not found in the freeze lists
Frozen.verdictClearText: Tether and Circle do not currently block this address (Ethereum, Tron, Arbitrum, Polygon, Base, Optimism, Avalanche). That does not make it safe: a freeze is only one of the checks.
Frozen.fullCheck: Full AML check of this address
Frozen.faq1a: Tether and Circle can block tokens at any address in their contracts. It usually happens at the request of law enforcement, because of sanctions or a link to fraud. The issuer does not disclose the reason.
Frozen.faq2q: Is a freeze the same as sanctions?
Frozen.faq2a: No. Sanctions are imposed by a government and addresses appear on official lists (OFAC and others). A freeze is made by the stablecoin issuer and can be lifted. See the Sanctions section for official lists.
Frozen.faq3a: Only through the issuer or a court. Only Tether or Circle can lift a block. If you own the address, contact their support with proof of identity and of where the funds came from.
Frozen.faq4q: Where does the list come from?
Frozen.faq4a: From the block and unblock events in the USDT and USDC contracts on chain. We take the latest event for each address, so an unblocked address is not listed.
